sights.w: Wright's only Prairie-style residence in Ohio (his first Ohio commission), designed 1906, built 1908, restored inch-by-inch in a $5.3M project reopened in 2005. On the National Register; hourly guided tours Tue-Sat 11-5, Sun 1-5. The marquee mid-corridor sight.

Depression-era folk-art masterpiece: unemployed molder Ben Hartman spent 1932-44 building a sprawling miniature world of hand-set stone and pebble monuments (Independence Hall, a castle, biblical and patriotic scenes) in his own yard. Preserved by the Kohler Foundation; free, open daily dawn-dusk. A nationally noted grassroots-art landmark.
The only Smithsonian Affiliate art museum in Ohio (affiliated since 2012). Regional collection strong on American art, plus rotating exhibitions, set at the edge of Cliff Park downtown.

The Clark County Historical Society's museum in Springfield's grand 1890 Romanesque former City Hall and Market House. Local history from the Ice Age through Springfield's industrial heyday (Rogers greeting cards, farm machinery), plus a cafe under the rotunda.

A Federal-style 1839 stagecoach tavern and inn built on the National Road, once a stopover for drovers and Conestoga-wagon pioneers. Saved from demolition by the DAR's Lagonda Chapter, run as a museum since 1941; on the National Register since 1973. Open limited days.

sights.n: George Rogers Clark Park & Battle of Peckuwe Site
sights.w: Riverside park on the site of the 1780 Battle of Peckuwe, the largest Revolutionary War engagement west of the Alleghenies, where Col. George Rogers Clark's forces met the Shawnee. Trails, monuments to Clark and Tecumseh, and the Davidson Interpretive Center (across Lower Valley Pike).

sights.address: W Main St at Fisher St (National Road Commons), Springfield, OH 45504
sights.w: The first of twelve identical DAR pioneer-mother monuments placed along the National Old Trails Road from Maryland to California, dedicated July 4, 1928 (Harry Truman attended). Springfield's was the first dedicated; moved in 2011 to National Road Commons downtown.

Restored formal gardens, arboretum and a Kiwanis children's garden within historic Snyder Park along Buck Creek, run by the National Trail Parks & Recreation District. Free public gardens, a horticulture and pollinator showcase.

sights.n: Buck Creek State Park / C.J. Brown Reservoir
sights.w: 1,900-acre ODNR park on the 2,120-acre C.J. Brown Reservoir just northeast of Springfield: swimming beach, marina, campground, cabins and trails, and a birding hotspot. From I-70 take Exit 59 north on SR-41.

sights.address: Indian Dr at Mound Circle, Enon, OH 45323
sights.w: Ohio's second-largest conical burial mound (after Miamisburg), about 40 ft high and 574 ft around, built by the Adena culture roughly 2,000 years ago and preserved on a residential circle in Enon. Owned by the village; free to view.
